name: ScyllaDB
use_case: Low-latency, high-throughput workloads (real-time analytics, IoT, ad-tech)
reasoning: ScyllaDB is a drop-in replacement for Apache Cassandra, re-implemented in C++ for lower latency and higher throughput. It keeps the same wide-column, partition/row data model and wire protocol, so it fits neatly into a single family: Wide-Column.

name: InfluxDB
use_case: Metrics, monitoring, sensor data, DevOps observability dashboards
reasoning: InfluxDB is purpose-built for time-series data with a SQL-like query language (InfluxQL/Flux). It behaves like a specialized Wide-Column store optimized purely for time-ordered writes and range scans, so it is best treated as its own Time-Series family rather than a generic Wide-Column store.

name: ArangoDB
data_model: JSON Document, Property Graph, Key-Value (single engine)
use_case: Applications needing documents, graph traversals, and key-value access without running three separate databases
reasoning: ArangoDB explicitly markets itself as a multi-model database: the same storage engine and query language (AQL) can store JSON documents, traverse graphs, and do simple key-value lookups. It deliberately spans three NoSQL families instead of fitting into one.
